# The closing run

For a cloud builder whose game is at its gates and whose design sheet has passed, when a message names this page. It is a short later run in the words of [`../CLOUD.md`](../CLOUD.md): fetch, switch to your branch, fast-forward to its remote tip. It makes the folder say what the game is, so that the lead can bring it into the jam as it stands. Build nothing new.

## What the run does

1. **Record the pass.** Read the last answers file for your game on the base branch. Write into the status block the round that passed, the checker, the hash it names and the commit that holds that sheet. Take out every line that still says an earlier round is open or that the sheet has not passed.
2. **The sheet part of `ART.md` (above `## The look`) says what the game does.** It has passed with a hash, so touch it only for this. Read it against the built game, sentence by sentence, as the reader will who goes through your code before the merge: every cell of the grid is both drawn and heard; every character has the moves and the tastes the sheet gives it, and "every time" means every time; every secret does what the sheet says; a sentence dropped or changed leaves no other mention of the old thing elsewhere in the sheet; and putting the game away in the middle of a drag or a scene makes no move the child did not make and replays nothing. Where a sentence promises something a child should see or hear and the game does not do it (a cell of the grid that sounds and is not drawn, or is drawn and has no sound; a secret; a move a character is said to have), the game is short, not the sheet: build it if it is a few lines, and otherwise list it under "Still weak" for the lead, who may hold the game back for it. Where a sentence only says a detail a little other than the game does (which place, which way, what a thing is made of) and the truth changes nothing of the mechanic, the error, the designed order, the saved state, the records or the claim, paste the sentence that is true, in every place the sheet says it. Then record the new sheet commit and hash in the status block, list each sentence you changed there (old and new), and set `Open: sheet ready for check, round N` with the next round's number. That round reads only those sentences; the lead has it done and records its outcome when the game is brought in, so the run does not wait for it. If you change no sentence, the passed hash stands and no round is asked for.
3. **Bring the rest into line with the built game.** Read `ART.md` below `## The look` and all of `REFINEMENT.md` from top to bottom, and correct every sentence that is no longer true: something "not built yet", "not started" or "coming later" that is built; what "this run" does not do; a file named that no longer exists; a count that has changed; a pointer to a heading that is not there. The pass log is history and stays as written; a row may get one closing clause where it would otherwise mislead.
4. **One fix in `audio.ts`**, which every game copied from the template before the template had it. A second finger or a palm lifting inside a touch must not end the wait the first finger started. In `GameAudio`: `private touching = false` becomes a count, `private touching = 0`; `touchDown` clears `held` only when the count is 0 and then adds one; `touchUp` takes one off when the count is above 0, instead of setting false; `play` tests `this.touching > 0`; `setActive(false)` sets the count to 0. Take the lines and the one new test ("keeps holding the first finger's sounds when a second finger or a palm lifts inside the touch") from `templates/cartridge/audio.ts` and `audio.test.ts` on the base branch (`git show origin/feat/learning-games-build:templates/cartridge/audio.ts`). If your `audio.ts` already counts, leave it.
5. **Commits.** A commit message ends with the one line `Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>`, with no other trailer and no web address.
6. **The checks** `CLOUD.md` names before a push and at a stage boundary. Then push and stop with the short report: the tip, what you changed, and anything you named for the lead.
